headline: GOLIATH SUREBET DRILLS 48,443 METRES IN 94 DAYS WITH 100% HIT RATE — DISCOVERY EXPANDS 12% TO 2.01 KM²
snippet: Goliath Resources Ltd. (TSX-V: GOT) concluded its 2026 season at the Golddigger Property in British Columbia's Golden Triangle having drilled 48,443 metres across 97 holes in 94 days — every single hole intercepting the targeted quartz-sulphide mineralization for a 100% hit rate — and expanded the Surebet Discovery footprint 12% to 2.01 km², with 46 stacked gold-rich veins now delineated across the Bonanza (1.51 km²) and Golden Gate (1.17 km²) zones. Preliminary metallurgical work achieved 92.2% gold recovery using simple gravity and flotation with no cyanide required — a significant processing advantage that materially reduces future capital and operating cost assumptions for a deposit in one of BC's premier high-grade gold districts.

headline: A2GOLD HITS 5.24% ANTIMONY AT NEVADA TAYLOR — 20.96 g/t AuEq AND 209 g/t Ag FROM SURFACE, 170M FROM PAST PRODUCER
snippet: A2Gold Corp. (TSX-V: AUAU, OTCQX: AUXXF) reported that holes TAR-008 and TAR-009 at the Taylor Silver-Gold Project in Nevada returned 20.96 g/t AuEq over 1.5 metres — including 5.24% antimony and 0.52 g/t gold — and 209.4 g/t silver over 10.7 metres from surface, with the antimony-gold intercept located 170 metres north of the past-producing Merrimac Mine. At a moment when US antimony prices are at record highs due to Chinese export controls, a domestic near-surface antimony-gold-silver system 170 metres from historical production is exactly the kind of strategic mineral asset that has attracted government financing interest and institutional attention in the current cycle.

headline: COPPER TESTS $6.75/LB NEAR RECORD AS GLOBAL MINE OUTPUT SET FOR FIRST DECLINE SINCE 2017
snippet: Copper advanced to $6.75/lb on Tuesday — within striking distance of the all-time LME record of $14,858/t ($6.74/lb) set on September 9 — as Sprott Asset Management warned that global mined copper output could decline year-on-year for the first time since 2017 due to production disruptions, deteriorating ore grades, and weak Chilean output, even as demand accelerates from power grid build-out, AI data centres, and defence. First-half 2026 mine production fell 1.1% year-on-year with an estimated 600,000-tonne output gap from disruptions in Indonesia and the DRC; the copper market is up 47% year-on-year and structurally tightening into the end of the decade.

headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,335 AS OIL'S 4-DAY SLIDE DAMPENS FED RATE HIKE BETS — SUMMIT BINARY STILL IN PLAY THURSDAY
snippet: Gold edged higher to approximately $4,335 on Tuesday as falling oil prices — down for four consecutive sessions on Middle East diplomatic progress and continued energy flows — reduced expectations for additional Federal Reserve rate hikes, offering a partial offset to hawkish statements from Feds Collins, Musalem, and Goolsbee, all of whom backed further tightening to address persistent commodity-driven inflation. Silver held near $65-66/oz; the gold-to-silver ratio is compressing slightly heading into Thursday's Trump-Xi summit, which remains the week's primary binary event for direction in precious metals.

headline: VISCOUNT DRILLS 473 g/t Ag AND 2.92 g/t Au OUTSIDE CURRENT RESOURCE — SILVER CLIFF COLORADO EXTENDS 1 KM FROM KATE BOUNDARY
snippet: Viscount Mining Corp. (CSE: VML, OTCQB: VLMGF) reported final assays from its 10-hole, 830-metre drill program at Silver Cliff in Colorado's Custer County, with all holes located outside the current Kate NI 43-101 resource and sites ranging from 68 metres to approximately 1 kilometre from the resource outline — confirming the Tr2/Tr3 silver-host rhyolites extend well beyond the currently defined boundary. The headline intercept of hole K26-08 hit 13.4 metres averaging 267.6 g/t silver including 7.9 metres at 473.2 g/t silver and 2.92 g/t gold, demonstrating that significant grade exists up to 1 km outside the currently classified resource — a strong signal for a coming resource expansion.

headline: I-80 GOLD EVERY STEP-OUT HOLE MINERALIZED AT MINERAL POINT — 225M AT 1.33 g/t Au, 39.2 g/t Ag IN NEVADA HEAP LEACH EXPANSION
snippet: i-80 Gold Corp. (TSX: IAU) announced initial 2026 assay results from infill and step-out drilling at the Mineral Point open pit heap leach project in Nevada, with all 19 step-out holes encountering mineralization and over half reporting more than 100 metres of gold and silver intercepts — headlined by a step-out hole of 225.6 metres at 1.33 g/t Au and 39.2 g/t Ag. The 100% step-out hit rate at significant widths across a heap leach target in Nevada — where permitting timelines are shorter and infrastructure is established — adds meaningful resource expansion potential to a project already within i-80's integrated Nevada gold production platform.

headline: SLAM HITS >1% ANTIMONY IN NEW BRUNSWICK TRENCHES — SKULL ZONE ADDS GOLD AND SILVER TO MOOSE LAKE STRATEGIC METALS SYSTEM
snippet: SLAM Exploration Ltd. (TSX-V: SXL, OTCQB: SXLXF) confirmed antimony greater than the 1% detection limit in three grab samples from trenches at the Skull epithermal zone of the Moose Lake project in New Brunswick — alongside grab samples returning up to 1.965 g/t gold and 73.50 g/t silver — establishing that the Skull zone hosts a multi-metal antimony-gold-silver system in addition to the copper-equivalent zone previously reported. The 3,895-hectare Moose Lake project, optioned in March 2026 and now showing multiple high-priority targets, positions SLAM in Canada's Atlantic antimony belt at a time when non-Chinese antimony supply is attracting acute strategic buyer interest.

headline: TINTINA FIRES 6 RIGS ON ATACAMA COPPER-GOLD — 40,000M DOS AMIGOS PROGRAM LAUNCHES, FIRST ASSAYS DUE MID-NOVEMBER
snippet: Tintina Mines Limited (TSX-V: TTS, OTCQB: TNNTF) announced the commencement of a 40,000-metre drill program at its 100%-owned Dos Amigos copper-gold project in Chile's Atacama Region, with up to six rigs expected on-site in Q4 2026 operating 24 hours a day through Q2 2027; initial assays are expected mid-November and an updated Mineral Resource Estimate is targeted for H2 2027. The program is designed to convert Inferred Mineral Resources to the Indicated category, forming the basis for future feasibility workstreams — and the Tricolor porphyry target, located 3km north, will be drill-tested in Q4 as a high-priority greenfield test in one of the world's most prolific copper belts.

headline: FROM SOYBEANS TO RARE EARTHS — EVERY COMMODITY MARKET BINARY IN THURSDAY'S TRUMP-XI SUMMIT EXPLAINED
snippet: Thursday's Washington summit between Trump and Xi places the tariff truce expiry (November 10), China's shortfall on rare earth and critical mineral deliveries from the Busan agreement, and rare earth magnets for EV motors and defense systems at the centre of the world's most consequential commodity trade negotiation — alongside soybeans (25M tonnes/year committed), LNG purchases, and a wider technology export-control framework. Agricultural commodities offer the easiest quick deal, while rare earths and antimony remain China's most potent industrial leverage — and the outcome is a direct binary for antimony, copper, and gold prices heading into the close of the week.

headline: CHINA'S 90% RARE EARTH PROCESSING GRIP PUTS EVERY EV MOTOR AND DEFENSE MAGNET AT STAKE IN THURSDAY'S SUMMIT
snippet: China controls approximately 90% of global rare earth refining and near-total processing of heavy rare earths including dysprosium and terbium that are essential for the permanent magnets in EV motors, wind turbines, and F-35 actuators — giving Beijing structural leverage at Thursday's summit that cannot be quickly substituted by Greenland access, Mountain Pass expansions, or Lynas output. For junior rare earth investors, a concrete Chinese commitment to resume certified delivery could immediately deflate the speculative premium that drove stocks like GRML +245% on Monday, while a breakdown would send it sharply higher — the binary is unusually clean.

headline: WHY GOLD ISN'T FOLLOWING REAL YIELDS HIGHER — THE DECOUPLING THAT'S CONFUSING BOND TRADERS IN 2026
snippet: Gold's stubborn refusal to fall materially despite real yields moving higher — the historical relationship that anchored every TIPS-based gold model from 2006 to 2022 — is generating the most visible analytical disagreement on the metal since 2020, with GoldSilver.com arguing that the decoupling reflects a structural shift in central bank demand, a loss of confidence in USD-denominated bond collateral after the Russian reserve seizures, and retail physical accumulation in Asia that operates on a different price-sensitivity curve than futures traders. For junior mining investors, this matters: if gold's floor is no longer set by real yield math, the downside scenarios that drive exploration company valuations need to be revised meaningfully upward.

headline: MARONAN METALS HITS COPPER-GOLD NORTH OF 32 MT RESOURCE — 26,000M STILL TO DRILL IN QUEENSLAND'S CLONCURRY BELT
snippet: Maronan Metals Ltd. (ASX: MMA) confirmed shallow copper-gold mineralisation extending north of the existing 32 Mt at 0.85% Cu, 0.63 g/t Au, 7 g/t Ag resource, with a novel copper intercept of 4.0 metres at 0.96% Cu associated with massive pyrrhotite at a location where copper had not previously been drilled — and 26,000 metres of a planned 40,000-metre 2026 campaign still to come, with 28 holes awaiting assay. The drill program is 65km south of Cloncurry in Queensland's prolific copper belt, and the shallow, high-grade extensions north of the resource boundary are consistent with the deposit geometry that has historically attracted producer interest in Australia's Eastern Succession.
